FRIDAY · NOV 27 · A GIANT FOREST ADVENTURE

A day among the sequoias

General Sherman and Congress Trail, sandwiches in Giant Forest, and Big Trees Trail if everyone still feels good.

◷ 7:30 AM departure · relaxed afternoon return♡  Main adventure🚗  CA-198 / Generals Highway
Outbound stops ↗Big Trees + hotel route ↗
✳
Morning go/no-go · please read before leaving

No scheduled Three Rivers break. Foothills Visitor Center is the first restroom stop. General Sherman and Congress Trail are the priorities; Big Trees Trail is a 0.7-mile optional loop after them. There is no hard pre-sunset hotel return: a relaxed start down from Giant Forest around 3:00–3:20 PM lets you approach the foothills near the 4:44 PM valley sunset, but mountain shade arrives earlier. NPS reports Moro Rock / Crescent Meadow Road closed to vehicles. Check chain rules on the park hotline (559) 565-3341 → 1 → 1; do not enter an active chain-control area without required traction equipment.

Wed Nov 25 · recentWintry conditions recently

Earlier NWS forecasts mentioned rain/snow risk. Exact snowfall at Sherman for Wednesday was not verified; NPS still displays a snow/ice caution.

Thu Nov 26 · todayMostly sunny → partly sunny

NWS zone forecast: about 42–56°F across Sequoia NP elevations. Not a reading at Sherman itself.

Fri Nov 27 · tomorrowMostly sunny → mostly cloudy

Forecast high range 36–54°F across the park; west/northwest gusts to around 20 mph. Friday night gustier.

Live park road status ↗Caltrans / CA-198 ↗NWS park forecast ↗Holiday shuttle ↗Only park stops route ↗Return to Fresno ↗Call road hotline ↗
Walking choices, not a forced hike. General Sherman and a comfortable portion of Congress Trail come first. The complete 2.7-mile Congress route plus the climb back to the parking lot can be tiring at altitude. Holiday shuttles run every 15 minutes from 10:00 AM–4:30 PM, Nov 26–29; Sherman parking can fill. Big Trees Trail is an optional bonus if the group still has energy and the trail is clear of snow and ice. Sandwiches are packed, and the hotel return is flexible.

Day highlights

7:30 AM
Departure7:30 AM

Leave Hampton Inn · Clovis

Direct to Sequoia on CA-198 · no planned Three Rivers stop

Head directly to Sequoia with sandwiches in a cooler, water, park pass, warm layers and footwear with good traction. Drive through Three Rivers without stopping unless somebody needs an unplanned break. Check chain-control information before leaving.

⌖Hampton Inn & Suites Clovis-Airport North, 855 Gettysburg Ave, Clovis, CA 93612
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Parking: Load everyone in the Hampton hotel parking lot; allow time for comfortable boarding.

Drive: Travel via Highway 99 / CA-198 toward Three Rivers and Ash Mountain. Allow roughly 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours to the park entrance, plus traffic.

Chain check: Call (559) 565-3341 and press 1, then 1. A highway being open does not rule out chain controls.

Restroom plan: Aim for Foothills Visitor Center, about a mile inside the entrance, instead of a separate Three Rivers break.

~9:15–9:30 AM
Entrance10–15 min allowance

Ash Mountain Entrance

Park entry on CA-198 / Generals Highway

Go through the south entrance, show your park pass or pay admission and ask about road and chain restrictions for the climb to Giant Forest. Slow holiday entry queues can shift the schedule.

⌖Ash Mountain Entrance Station, Sequoia National Park, CA
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Chain decision: Ask whether a front-wheel-drive Camry can proceed to Giant Forest / Sherman without installing chains or cables.

Direction: Stay on paved Generals Highway. Foothills Visitor Center is approximately one mile past the entrance.

Timing: If the entrance takes longer than planned, skip Hospital Rock before cutting your priorities.

~9:35–9:55 AM
Visitor center15–20 min

Foothills Visitor Center

One mile past the entrance · planned restroom stop

Take your first proper bathroom and orientation break here. Ask about Sherman parking, accessibility/shuttles, icy trails and whether Big Trees Trail is in good condition. Pick up a map or ask for a temporary accessible-parking pass if appropriate.

⌖Foothills Visitor Center, 47050 Generals Highway, Three Rivers, CA 93271
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Parking: Use the signed Foothills Visitor Center lot directly off Generals Highway.

Comfort: Low-effort restroom and seated break before the long curvy mountain ascent.

Best questions: “Are Sherman, Congress and Big Trees trails free of ice? Which parking lot or shuttle minimizes walking for somebody with limited mobility?”

Hours: Park facility hours may vary seasonally; if closed, use any available exterior facilities and proceed as conditions permit.

~10:05–10:15 AM
Optional view5–10 min

Hospital Rock · optional scenic pause

Kaweah River canyon · near roadside

A quick look at the foothill scenery, if everyone feels good. Skip this stop entirely if you want more time among the giant sequoias or the mountain drive is taking longer.

⌖Hospital Rock Picnic Area, Sequoia National Park, CA
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Parking: Use signed picnic-area parking, never the roadway shoulder.

Mobility: Stay on stable, level surfaces; avoid descending to the river or climbing uneven rocks.

Priority: This is skippable. Sherman and Congress remain your must-dos.

~10:55–11:15 AM
Forest orientation15–20 min

Giant Forest Museum · orientation

Near Big Trees Trail access · check ranger guidance

Brief stop at the museum area to see the sequoias and locate the Big Trees Trail access for later. If parking is packed, ask a ranger or use the Thanksgiving shuttle and adapt your order.

⌖Giant Forest Museum, Sequoia National Park, CA
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Parking: Signed Giant Forest Museum lots; NPS warns parking here and at Sherman fills early on Thanksgiving weekend.

Accessibility: The main parking across the road has accessible restroom facilities; use the signed crossings.

Big Trees access: Trailhead about 0.3 mile from the museum, so the full Round Meadow walk requires an additional connector unless eligible for closer parking.

Shuttles: Fare-free holiday shuttle service Nov 26–29, 10 AM–4:30 PM, about every 15 minutes; confirm the route at the stop.

~11:20–11:45 AM
Packed lunch20–25 min

Sandwich picnic · Pinewood

Packed lunch in Giant Forest · no restaurant detour

Eat the sandwiches you brought from Fresno. Pinewood Picnic Area is about one mile north of the museum and on the way toward Sherman. Use this if the picnic area is open and safe; otherwise eat at another signed picnic spot or from the legally parked vehicle.

⌖Pinewood Picnic Area, Sequoia National Park, CA
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Parking: Use signed Pinewood Picnic Area parking. NPS lists accessible parking, a picnic table, and vault toilets; winter access and snow clearance are not guaranteed.

Food safety: Keep perishable sandwiches cool until eating. Pack all trash out and never leave food unattended around wildlife.

Route: Pinewood is on Generals Highway approximately one mile north of Giant Forest Museum; continue toward Sherman afterwards.

Fallback: If Pinewood is closed, have the sandwiches at a legal parking/picnic area near Giant Forest Museum instead.

~11:55 AM–12:45 PM
Must-see~50–65 min

General Sherman Tree

Your top priority · the world’s largest tree by volume

Park or take a holiday shuttle and enjoy time at General Sherman. From the main lot the paved trail is about 0.5 mile downhill to the tree and requires a climb back; leave enough energy for that return. The accessible lower trailhead offers a much shorter approach if you qualify.

⌖General Sherman Tree Main Trailhead, Sequoia National Park, CA
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Parking: General Sherman Main Trailhead lot off Wolverton Road was listed open, but holiday crowds may fill it.

Mobility: For the lower accessible trailhead, use permitted accessible parking or seek guidance on a temporary access pass. The holiday shuttle can also help reduce walking.

Walking: Standard main path is ~0.5 mile one-way, descending toward the tree. Budget the uphill return and possible icy surfaces.

Photography: Take your time here: it is the must-see stop, so do not sacrifice it to make the optional trail.

~12:45–1:35 PM
Must-see trail~40–50 min partial

Congress Trail · explore at your pace

Starts right beside General Sherman · no second parking

Walk a comfortable portion of the paved Congress Trail past immense sequoias and turn around whenever anyone is tired. The complete route is about 2.7 miles round-trip and can take substantially longer with breaks; make a partial walk the default, with the full loop only if everyone has the stamina and the trail is clear of ice.

⌖Congress Trailhead beside General Sherman Tree, Sequoia National Park, CA
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Trailhead: Begin on foot immediately beside General Sherman; no new driving directions or parking lot.

Choice: Short out-and-back: 20–50 minutes. The entire 2.7-mile route requires extra time and may push Big Trees out of the plan.

Mobility: Paved but not completely flat; elevations and ice make progress slower. Turn back whenever comfortable.

Return: Leave enough time to reach the main parking lot or accessible shuttle stop again before moving to the next area.

~1:35–2:05 PM
Rest + transfer20–30 min

Return to your car or shuttle

Sherman uphill return · take it slowly

Walk back from the Sherman/Congress area, or board the appropriate accessible shuttle. No hard cutoff now: this break gives everyone time to recover before deciding whether Big Trees Trail sounds enjoyable.

⌖General Sherman Tree Main Trailhead, Sequoia National Park, CA
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Return climb: The standard route back from Sherman gains elevation, so pace yourself and rest as needed.

Shuttle: If your group parked farther out, allow time for the free holiday shuttle and confirm when the final return service runs.

Decision: If everyone is tired, skip Big Trees Trail and start the scenic return drive.

~2:10–3:00 PM
Optional scenic walk40–60 min with access

Big Trees Trail · optional Round Meadow loop

0.7-mile paved loop with benches · near Giant Forest Museum

One last peaceful grove experience, only if everyone still has energy. The flat, paved Big Trees Trail circles Round Meadow and offers plenty of photo opportunities and benches. It is about 0.7 mile as a loop, plus the approach from the museum lot if you park there. You can also peek at the meadow and head back without doing the full loop.

⌖Big Trees Trailhead, Sequoia National Park, CA
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Regular parking: Use the signed lot across from Giant Forest Museum and walk roughly 0.3 mile to the trailhead, then back again. Full loop plus connector is around 1.3 miles total.

Accessible parking: A small closer lot is designated for visitors with qualifying placards or passes. Ask staff about a temporary pass if mobility needs warrant one; winter rules can differ.

Difficulty: Paved loop, little elevation change and benches, but snow/ice can still make the path unsuitable.

Skip rule: Treat this as a bonus; stop early if Congress took longer than expected, the surface is icy or someone needs rest.

~3:00–3:20 PM
Scenic returnPlan ~1–1.5 hr to foothills

Begin the scenic descent

Aim for lower foothills near sunset · no rush

Drive down Generals Highway at a comfortable pace. The road has many switchbacks, and mountain shade arrives before the official valley sunset. If you depart Giant Forest around 3–3:20 PM, you may be near the Ash Mountain foothills around sunset, depending on traffic and road conditions. This is a flexible target—not a deadline.

⌖Giant Forest → Ash Mountain / CA-198 → Clovis, CA
Get directions ↗
Parking & access ⌄

Sunset: Official Fresno sunset Friday Nov 27 is about 4:44 PM. Shaded portions of Generals Highway can darken much earlier.

Driving: Do not speed to chase sunset. If anyone feels unwell, make a legal pullout stop.

Winter roads: Conditions may change during the day. If snow, ice or chain controls worsen, follow ranger instructions and adjust departure earlier.

No closed road detours: Moro Rock / Crescent Meadow Road remains closed to vehicles due to recent snow; stay on the open paved route.

~6:00–6:45 PM
Hotel returnEstimated arrival

Back at Hampton Inn · relax

Sunset on the drive is okay · rest before dinner

Return to your hotel in Clovis whenever the mountain descent and road traffic allow. Being back before sundown is no longer the goal—enjoy the afternoon, drive safely and relax after the trip.

Before you go

Roads & comfort

🌲 Friday: check Sequoia roads by 6:45 AM

Call (559) 565-3341 (press 1 then 1). Routes may be open yet under active chain controls; do not proceed into a controlled segment without required equipment. Moro Rock / Crescent Meadow closed to vehicles.

🌅 Saturday: sunset around 4:43 PM

Leave Woodward by 2:35 PM. Skip an optional stop if needed to get to Millerton before dark.

💛 Mobility-first

Accessible parking and restrooms when available, layers for cold mornings, and no mandatory hikes. Check holiday business hours.
